newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific earnings rise, stock rallies.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific earnings rise, stock rallies.

text.p: Union Pacific Corp., which completed its $5.4 billion merger with Southern Pacific Corp. last month, Thursday said earnings rose 16 percent in the third quarter, in line with expectations on Wall Street.

The nation's biggest railroad, which also just completed the spin-off of its energy operations, said net income rose to $275 million, or $1.30 a share, in the quarter, from $237 million, or $1.15 a share, in the 1995 period.
Sales edged up to $2.0 billion from $1.97 billion.
The Bethlehem, Pa.-based company cited strong results at its railroad, where operating earnings jumped 11 percent on a 3 percent rise in carloadings and improved productivity.

The results included income from Union Pacific Resources Group Inc., the 83-percent owned energy and natural resources subsidiary that was split into a separate company and distributed to Union Pacific Corp. shareholders on Tuesday.
Excluding Union Pacific Resources, income from continuing operations rose 32 percent to $211 million, or $1 a share, from $160 million, or 78 cents a share, Union Pacific said.
Analysts had forecast earnings of $1 a share for continuing operations, according to First Call, which tracks estimates.
While results were about as expected, Union Pacific stock jumped $2.50 to $53.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.

"We were pleased with the corporation's strong financial results," Chief Executive Officer Drew Lewis said in a statement. "When combined with the spin-off of our resources company and the completion of our Southern Pacific merger, it was a great quarter on all fronts for Union Pacific."

Earnings from Southern Pacific offset higher interest costs related to the acquisition, which was completed on Sept. 11, Union Pacific said. Southern Pacific results will be fully consolidated with Union Pacific as of Oct. 1.
While the financial merger has been completed, combining the operations of the two railroads -- which together have 31,000 miles of track -- will take at least two years, the company has said.
